review_state: production rev 1 - M1, awaiting owner look review
purpose: Creature world tree (PROPOSED, original): an umbrella tree about 7.6 m tall with a bulbous, buttressed trunk and a broad layered umbrella crown of leaf-spray cards.

textures.name: T_CreatureTreeUmbrella_ORM
textures.packing: R occlusion, G roughness, B metallic

textures.name: T_TreeCanopyCards
textures.packing: RGB the authored colour (CIE LCh greens and turquoise at hue 155 to 176, stems a low-chroma brown) in a 2 x 2 grid of 512 px cells: 0 umbrella spray; 1 umbrella spray fine; 2 lantern curtain; 3 lantern cap; A the cut-out mask (alpha scissor at 0.5)

pivot: the trunk's foot on the ground (Godot y = 0); the roots sink about 10 cm so the tree sits into a slope
placement: an obstacle: OUTSIDE the walls only (the berm and the hills, where max(|x|, |z|) is 80.5 m or more, crown included) until the sim has obstacles (issue #210); tests/test_creature_world_art.gd keeps anything over 0.45 m out of the walkable field

canopy.material: M_TreeCanopyCards (StandardMaterial3D: alpha scissor 0.5, back faces culled, COLOR_0 jitter)
canopy.sides: two sheets back to back per card, opposite winding
canopy.normals: out of the crown's ellipsoid plus 0.45 x world up on both sheets, so the crown shades as one rounded volume
canopy.lods: none (Godot's LOD pass collapses whole cards)

reduction.method: Blender collapse decimation to the triangle budget; the full-detail shape and shader relief baked to the normal map

provenance: Authored procedurally by tools/blender/creature_flora.py (through make_creature_world.py); no external or generated meshes. The wood is a skin-modifier skeleton baked in Blender from procedural shaders; the canopy card atlas is painted in numpy (strokes in CIE LCh); no scans.
